case_name: Toguru Sudhakar Reddy and Another v Government of A. P. and Others
facts: The Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Societies Act, 1964 was amended in the year 1991 and a proviso was added to Section 31(1)(a) of the said Act.

The above quoted proviso was challenged by the appellants-petitioners before the Andhra Pradesh High Court on the ground that it was arbitrary and as such violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India.
Rules 22(c) and 22-A(3)(a) which were added by the Notification dated March 20, 1991 were also challenged on similar grounds.
The State Government in the counter-affidavit filed before the High Court justified the enactment of the impugned provisions on the following grounds:

There are very few women members who have contested elections at the village level to gain entry into the managing committee of the societies and influence the decision-making process of the committee.
issues: Whether the proviso added to Section 31(1)(a) of the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Societies Act, 1964 was arbitrary and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India.
Whether the reservation beyond 50 per cent. was permissible.
petitioner_arguments: The proviso added to Section 31(1)(a) of the Andhra Pradesh Cooperative Societies Act, 1964 was arbitrary and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India.
Rules 22(c) and 22-A(3)(a) which were added by the Notification dated March 20, 1991 were also challenged on similar grounds.
respondent_arguments: The amendment was introduced to give representation to women in the managing committee of the societies.

Even though there are women members in the societies, they are not coming forward to contest elections to the societies, which invariably involve serious campaigning on the basis of factional and political consideration.
court_reasoning: The High Court rejected the main contention of the appellants-petitioners on the reasoning that Article 15(3) of the Constitution of India permits the making of special provisions for women.
The High Court went into the scheme of the Andhra Pradesh Co-operative Societies Act, 1964 in detail and came to the conclusion that impugned provisions were not arbitrary.
holding: We dismiss the appeals with no order as to costs.
